mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate investments, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower in tightening periods compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates a strengthening demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator for overall economic growth, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns do not show a significant positive trend during periods of increasing housing starts (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3 percentage points within the last month signals a tightening labor market, which increases wage pressures and corporate costs, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly lower in periods of decreasing unemployment compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% within the last two months signals increased economic activity, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns do not show a significant positive trend during periods of increasing industrial production (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) and a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) over the last month signals a strengthening consumer demand and a tightening labor market, which together boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increase & UNRATE decrease in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns do not show a significant positive trend during periods of increasing consumption and decreasing unemployment (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% within the last two months signals a potential deflationary pressure, which increases real interest rates and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower in periods of decreasing CPI compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 over the last month signals a strong labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns do not show a significant positive trend during periods of strong payroll growth (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in real GDP (GDPC1) indicates a strengthening economy, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, especially during an early-cycle expansion.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns do not show a significant positive trend during periods of increasing real GDP (t-test p > 0.05).
